sections.h2: Who records deeds in Champaign County?
sections.html:
The Champaign County Clerk and Recorder records deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and other land documents. Until 2020 the Recorder was a separate elected office. Voters approved a merger that year, and on January 1, 2022 it became the combined Clerk and Recorder's office. The office dates to 1833, the year the county was organized, and it keeps the land ownership records that title companies search before a sale.

Land records are open to the public, with Social Security numbers, phone numbers and email addresses redacted. In person, the office is open Monday through Friday from 8 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon, excluding major holidays, with a 9 o'clock opening on the second Wednesday of each month.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Champaign County?
sections.html:
A standard real estate document costs $70 to record, with no additional page charge. That covers deeds, mortgages and releases that meet the office's formatting rules. The fee schedule posted by the office, effective April 1, 2025, is below.

Champaign County Clerk and Recorder fee schedule as of April 1, 2025
Document typeRecording fee
Standard real estate documents$70.00
Non-standard real estate documents$82.00
Power of attorney$51.00
UCC original, amendment or continuation$33.00
UCC termination$13.00
Government agencies and municipalities$51.00

The office's file-records page announces that recording fees will rise by $10 on December 1, 2026, so confirm the current figure before you send a check. Plain copies run $.50 per page, and certified copies cost $12 for the first four pages and $1 for each additional page. Government bodies are exempt from the $19 Rental Housing Support fee, which lowers their total by that amount.

sections.h2: How should a deed be prepared for recording in Champaign County?
sections.html:
A deed that misses a formatting rule is billed at the non-standard rate or sent back. The office lists these requirements for real estate documents:

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, with the top 3 by 5 inches on the right side left blank.
  • No permanently bound or continuous forms, and nothing stapled or taped to a page.
  • The full name and address of the preparer, and of the place to return the document, within the text.
  • Original signatures and correct payment by check or cash.
  • For deeds, a complete name and address for where the tax bill is to be sent.
  • An associated document number for assignments and releases.

Plat rules are numerous, and the office advises asking your surveyor. The tax bill address on the deed matters because the Treasurer's office warns that a bill can still reach the previous owner when the closing date and recording date fall on different sides of a billing cycle.

sections.h2: What is MyDec and why does every Champaign County deed need it?
sections.html:
MyDec is the Illinois Department of Revenue's free online service for transfer declarations and revenue stamps, and Champaign County processes all property transactions through it. Every deed needs a signed and dated State of Illinois MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption. Sign up on the Department's site before closing day, because the declaration is part of the package the recorder checks.

Electronic recording is the fast route. Documents e-recorded through an approved partner are submitted over the internet, recorded and returned digitally the same day. The partners listed by the office are ePN, Indecomm Global Services, Simplifile, CSC eRecording Solutions and Hopdox. The office lists fewer rejections, quicker corrections and savings on postage among the benefits, so ask your title company or closing attorney whether they e-record.

sections.h2: How much is the Illinois transfer tax on a Champaign County sale?
sections.html:
Illinois imposes a tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, stated in the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). When the transferring document says the property is transferred subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis. The tax is due whether or not a document is recorded.

The recorder collects it through revenue stamps. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, and counties issue electronic stamps or alternative indicia afterward, reporting through MyDec. Ask the Clerk and Recorder or your title company which local charges, if any, appear on your settlement statement.

Section 31-45 lists deeds exempt from the tax. These are some of them:

  • Deeds to or from a governmental body, or from certain charitable, religious or educational organizations.
  • Deeds that secure a debt, and deeds that release property held as security.
  • Deeds that only confirm, correct or supplement a deed already recorded.
  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Tax deeds, deeds of partition, and deeds given to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.

Some exempt deeds still need the declaration filed, so check the statute text before skipping the form.

sections.h2: What does Champaign County look like for people recording a sale?
sections.html:
Champaign County had an estimated 209,972 residents by mid-2025, across about 996 square miles, and the Census Bureau shows 54.0% of housing units owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024. A typical owner-occupied home was valued at $211,500, and the median gross rent was $1,051. Urbana is the seat, Champaign is the largest city, and the University of Illinois sits between them.

The Clerk and Recorder works from the county's Urbana offices, while the Treasurer collects the tax on the same parcels. A student rental in Champaign, a ranch house in Mahomet and a farm parcel near a village will each record the same way, but their prior-owner tax bills and any unpaid installments can differ widely. Pull the PIN history from the Treasurer before the deed goes in.

sections.h2: What happens after the deed is recorded in Champaign County?
sections.html:
Recording moves the property into the new owner's name in the land records, and the tax side follows separately. The Champaign County Treasurer tells new owners to check their closing documents, title company or attorney to see whether tax is owed. If the bill went to the previous owner, that person has to forward it, and the Treasurer will send a duplicate on request at 217-384-3743.

A seller who wants a clean exit should confirm that both installments for the year are paid or credited on the settlement statement. Unpaid taxes become part of the annual sale in late October, and redemption after a sale runs through the County Clerk, so a missed payment turns into a second office visit later.

sections.h2: What else does the recorder's office handle?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the office accepts veterans' DD-214 discharge papers at no charge. A veteran brings the original, the staff scan it, create a permanent record and return the original. A certified copy later requires a government-issued ID, and military discharge papers less than 62 years old are not available to the public.

State and federal tax liens and releases are recorded for $51 each. Releases of a mortgage you paid off are recorded here too, and a release needs the document number of the mortgage it satisfies. Before listing a house, ask your title company to search for open mortgages and liens so a release can be recorded ahead of closing.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Champaign County?
faqs.a: $70 for a standard real estate document, or $82 if it misses one of the office's requirements. The office has announced a $10 increase effective December 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Do I need a MyDec declaration to record a deed in Champaign County?
faqs.a: Yes. Every deed needs a signed and dated MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption, and the county runs all property transactions through MyDec.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Champaign County?
faqs.a: Yes. Approved partners such as Simplifile, ePN and CSC eRecording submit documents over the internet, and they are recorded and returned the same day.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. Mortgage balances left in place are excluded from the basis.

faqs.q: When is the recorder's office open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, closed on major holidays. On the second Wednesday of each month the doors open at 9.
